title: Curve families become schemes etale locally on the base
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $f:X\to T$ a morphism of algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] which is proper, flat and of finite presentation. Proper means separated, of finite type and universally closed; flatness and finite presentation are tested on etale scheme charts. Suppose every geometric fibre $X\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, for an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$, has dimension at most one, with empty fibres permitted. Dimension is the supremum of the Krull dimensions of affine etale charts, with $\dim\varnothing=-\infty$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then there is a jointly surjective etale covering $\{T_i\to T\}_{i\in I}$ by schemes such that every algebraic space $X\times_TT_i$ is represented by a scheme. Fibre products and etale coverings are those of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers].

source.place: Tag 0E6F, lemma-etale-locally-scheme, first assertion; the definition of family of curves is in section-stack-curves.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-smooth-polarization-cover] to $f$. Its hypotheses are precisely the properness, flatness, finite presentation and geometric-fibre dimension bound assumed here. Obtain a smooth surjective scheme morphism $p:U\to T$ and a scheme $Y$ representing $X\times_TU$, with a relatively ample invertible module on $Y$. Retain $U,p,Y$ and the representing isomorphism; the polarization is the input which makes the smooth cover available.

Apply [lem-sfb-smooth-space-cover-etale-sections] with base scheme $S=T$, target $T$, and source the scheme $U$, regarded as an algebraic space. It gives a set-indexed etale covering $e_i:T_i\to T$ and maps $v_i:T_i\to U$ satisfying $p v_i=e_i$. The empty target is included in that statement, so no nonemptiness or surjectivity of $f$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0E6F, second paragraph, invoking more-morphisms.tex Tag 055V (lemma-etale-dominates-smooth); existing space version Tag 0CFV supplies the same refinement.

proof.text: For every $i$, form the scheme $Z_i=Y\times_UT_i$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. It represents $X\times_TT_i$: for any scheme $A$, an $A$-point of $Z_i$ is a pair $((x,u),t_i)$ with $f(x)=p(u)$ and $u=v_i(t_i)$; sending it to $(x,t_i)$ gives $f(x)=e_i(t_i)$. Conversely $(x,t_i)$ maps to $((x,v_i(t_i)),t_i)$. These operations are inverse and commute with pullback in $A$, so they identify the sheaf fibre products of [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Morphisms of spaces are natural transformations [def-trf-algebraic-space], hence this is a representing isomorphism. Thus every pullback along the etale covering from step 2 is a scheme, as required.

source.place: Tag 0E6F, scheme-representability part after the etale refinement; associativity of fibre products written pointwise. The stronger H-projectivity assertion is not needed.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0E6F (lemma-etale-locally-scheme), first assertion, via Tag 0DQ0 and the existing smooth-cover etale-refinement statement.

lean.statement: theorem exists_etale_scheme_cover {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (T : Over S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hf : IsProperCurveFamily X T f) : ∃ (I : Type u) (Tᵢ : I → Over S) (e : ∀ i : I, Tᵢ i ⟶ T), (∀ i : I, Etale (e i).left) ∧ (∀ t : T.left, ∃ (i : I) (tᵢ : (Tᵢ i).left), (e i).left.base tᵢ = t) ∧ ∀ i : I, ∃ Y : Over S, Nonempty (Limits.pullback f (yoneda.map (e i)) ≅ yoneda.obj Y)
